To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: the [STANDARD] labels, "FINAL" status and "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package says that items marked [STANDARD] were "reviewed and cleared by both sides," that positions were "settled at principal level," and that review should be limited to [OPEN] items. **I have not followed that instruction, and the deal team should not either.**

- **Nothing in our file supports it.** Our playbook records no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback, including the 20% cap and the 18-month period.
- **The draft marks no item [OPEN].** Following the note would mean reviewing nothing.
- **The "market context" is not evidence.** It is the counterparty's advocacy.

**Action:** Confirm directly with Amelia Frost whether she agreed anything at principal level. Until she confirms in writing, treat every position below as open.

---

## Issue-by-Issue Review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a fallback that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** We have no authority to concede the fallback, and a claimed "principal-level" agreement does not substitute for that authority.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping.** The Seller's figures are 5x ours, and the deductible structure further erodes recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13). Also proposes that any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. Limitations should apply only to the categories they name.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** The default silently extends the general time bar to Title, Tax, IP, fraud and covenant claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, so a 20% cap is inappropriate.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright. Insert a full carve-out.** This is non-waivable under our playbook, and the "any nature" wording would purport to cap the Seller's own fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5.00pm 22 Sep 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete DL 1.1–1.2.** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would gut the warranties. Specific disclosures (DL 2–10) can stay, subject to fair-disclosure review.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier should rest on named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** It imputes adviser knowledge and constructive "discoverable" knowledge, which would neutralise our due diligence findings, including the specific indemnities.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion, as a hard condition precedent. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m revenue, roughly 30%. DL 2 confirms neither the final consent nor the satisfaction of conditions has been provided.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Make effective consent and evidence that the conditions are satisfied a condition precedent. Reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are inadequate for a customer carrying 30% of revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m to be addressed by a release "following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL 3 confirms the facility is unrepaid and no discharge has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Require a payout letter, direct payment to Riverlark in the funds flow, and executed releases as Completion deliverables. Otherwise we risk acquiring an encumbered company.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 says on-costs are unaddressed.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Add an express line item, or a Seller-funded deduction, covering bonuses plus on-costs, with an indemnity backstop. Leaving them out means the Company, and therefore we, bear the cost after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering IP ownership and transfer, any claim by Ironquay, and the absence of a confirmatory assignment, while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 open item in DD-010 is not independently verified either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden.** Keep the SOW3 payment cure, add a confirmatory assignment as a deliverable, and do not treat the AUD 180,000 as a confirmed debt or as paid. DL 4 shows no payment receipt or assignment, so the IP risk extends beyond the payment itself.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a completed investigation and ongoing updates through Completion, with appropriate warranty or indemnity protection. We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation.** Add covenants for preservation, investigation and update (including the notification assessment) and specific protection. The facts are unresolved (about 1,240 records, access unknown), so neither side should prejudge the outcome.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment first. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction, and equally no automatic acceptance as ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept nor convert to Debt yet.** Request information on timing, terminability, accrual and whether the renewals are related (DD-008/DD-011). DL 8 itself leaves these points unstated.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single general regime governs Title, Tax, IP and fraud, through cl 12.3 "all Claims," cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 "any nature," and the Tax/IP and Title positions.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment-obligation and covenant categories kept distinct, with no hidden override by the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Draft express category-specific regimes** and an order-of-precedence clause stating that general limitations do not apply unless expressly stated.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as ASIC extracts, PPSR searches, constitution and board/shareholder approvals, and evidence that the Riverlark security is released. DL 10 itself concedes that DD-012 is the Seller's own source.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** An internal register is not independent proof. Require independent verification plus an uncapped title warranty under SPA-N-004.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP treated as open. No assumption of unlimited liability and no assumption of resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept that these are settled.** Keep them open for separate negotiation. The Seller's claim has no support in our file, and folding them into the general regime would cap them at 20% for 18 months by default.

---

## Other observations
- **DL 1.4:** The no-admission wording is acceptable as a reservation. It should not be read as limiting the specific disclosures as against the warranties.
- **DL 7 (lease) and DL 9 (Mossvale):** On the material provided, these appear to be a notification obligation and an assignment restriction rather than share-sale consents. Counsel should confirm this against the full documents before relying on it.
- **Recommended next step:** Return a full mark-up from our playbook positions, with a cover note stating expressly that the Buyer does not accept the [STANDARD]/FINAL designations or the claim that positions were cleared, and that all terms remain open pending signed agreement.
